anomalies.finding: find_skill coverage curve FLAT at N=3/5/8
anomalies.explanation: find_skill(limit=8) returns at most 3 results for all 22 session_start queries. Root cause: the 0.48 relevance threshold (RetrievalConfig.relevance_threshold) filters all candidates below the semantic score floor. The production retrieval pipeline applies this threshold before the limit cap. Therefore the diagnostic coverage curve is identical at N=3, 5, and 8 — the ceiling is the threshold, not the window. T12 bounded-set design must account for this: expanding N alone gains nothing; threshold relaxation or recurrence-signal re-ranking is required.

anomalies.finding: Verbose substratum p95 latency BREACH (734ms > 500ms guardrail)
anomalies.explanation: The verbose substratum p95 latency is 734ms, breaching the 500ms guardrail. The two outliers are t18-session-start-verbose-docker-build-failure-musl (734ms, 1501-char text) and t18-session-start-verbose-harness-agent-eval (608ms, 669-char). Long queries require more embedding time. This is a pre-T12 latency finding — the guardrail applies to the production SessionStart surface, not just thin queries.

anomalies.finding: Verbose no_match rate LOWER than thin (0.091 vs 0.182)
anomalies.explanation: Contrary to T14 smoke Finding-2 expectation, verbose queries have a lower no_match rate than thin (1/11 = 9.1% vs 2/11 = 18.2%). However verbose coverage@3 is dramatically lower (0.0274 vs 0.1096) — the verbose queries DO retrieve skills but they retrieve the WRONG ones (low gold overlap). The no_match threshold is not firing on verbose length, but the semantic signal is degraded by topic density.
